harness.description: Isolated reproduction of the suspected midday pattern: an invoice is finalized (status 'unpaid', auto-commit, through a shared query helper) before its generate-invoice job is enqueued. Not midday's code.

environment.networkIsolation: sandbox-exec: IP networking denied; Unix sockets and file writes limited to the replay directory
environment.database: ephemeral-postgres: private cluster, Unix socket only (listen_addresses=''), trust authentication for a local test user, fresh database per run, deleted afterwards

cases.description: The process dies after the status update committed and before the job is enqueued.

injection.description: After `db.update(invoices)` (step 0) commits and before `triggerJob("generate-invoice", …)` (step 1) is performed.

simulation.claim: If the process dies right after step 0: durable or visible: `db.update(invoices)` (step 0); never performed: `triggerJob("generate-invoice", …)` (step 1).
notModeled: Exceptions: an injected exception runs catch/finally handlers and transaction rollbacks in the application, which the model does not execute; only a process crash is simulated.
Effects of unknown operations, and the database's own failure modes (failed commits, isolation anomalies).
Anything outside the analyzed function: retries, reconciliation jobs, relays, consumers.

assumptions: `db.update(invoices)` runs outside any transaction: it commits on its own when its awaited promise resolves (auto-commit).
`triggerJob("generate-invoice", …)` becomes visible to other systems when its call completes.
`db.update(invoices)` is recognized by name-based match against the configuration (`db`); the analysis does not check types.
`triggerJob("generate-invoice", …)` is recognized by name-based match against the configuration (`triggerJob`); the analysis does not check types.
The application's invariants are unknown: the trace shows that the partial state can arise, not that it violates a business rule.
limitations: CommitRift does not know the application's invariants or what code outside this function does; a retry, reconciliation job, or idempotent consumer elsewhere may already repair this state.
This trace is a static candidate: no application code was executed to produce it.
